OLX Gang

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We expose a dangerous syndicate who hold innocent victims who advertised vehicles for sale online, hostage at gunpoint and force them to empty out their bank accounts.

Unique Selling Point:
We have been approached by two case studies who have fallen victim to a syndicate using the exact same modus operandi to rob them. The syndicate approaches people who have advertised vehicles for sale online via sites like OLX and Gumtree. They employ the exact same tactics every time. A coloured man who speaks fluent afrikaans phones the victim, and he claims to be in South Africa from Namibia. He offers to buy the vehicle at the advertised price, but tells the victims they have to meet him in Van der Bijl Park as he is only in the country for a short time and does not have transport. He assures them he does not need to see the vehicle, and that he is a truck driver, and will come pick up the vehicle with the truck on the next visit to SA.

Summary:
He asks them to remove the ads online. He tells them to meet him at a shopping center in Van der Bijl Park where they can sign a sales contract and he will pay the money over to their accounts. Once they meet him at the shopping centre the story changes. He shows them a large amount of cash, and says he will pay them cash, but that they have to go fetch the rest of the money at a friend's house. They then drive him to a house (that we have identified) in Evaton. Once inside they show the victims another bag which supposedly contains rough diamonds and asks them if they will be interested in taking the diamonds as payment. At this point two men, dressed in full police uniforms appear, and accuse the victims of being involved in diamond smuggling. They separate the victims into two rooms, where they are told they will be taken to police station and repeatedly raped if they do not cooperate. They are physically assaulted and have guns pointed at them. They are then forced to transfer money from their bank accounts into the syndicates bank accounts. The syndicate also takes their bank cards to atms and withdraws cash. If the limits are reached, the syndicate will hold one victim hostage while another is driven to a bank where they are forced to withdraw any remaining funds under threat of having the remaining victim at the house shot. Once the victims have been robbed, they are let go, and warned that if they go to police they will be killed. The syndicate has their registration nr on their vehicle checked, and obtain personal info like street address and such about the victims. They are then told the usual "we know where you live"...

Further information:
We have identified the house where the syndicate operates from(at least in our two cases studies incidents)

We have approached the Hawks organised crime unit via Gen Mokotedi and a Col Frik Smit. They have given the green light to go ahead with a sting/ bust, but they have not responded since and don't seem to be in much of a hurry to help us.

So then we approached members of Crime Intelligence, who are willing to setup the sting with us. They have a hand picked unit made up of police from different units who could carry out the sting and make the arrests. We are meeting with them on monday afternoon, we are going to film the briefing session with presenter. They are adamant that the sting can happen soon, but want as much info from us as possible.

One of our case studies, Chris van den Berg, has since it happened to him posted fake ads online and been contacted by the same gang. He has agreed to help us post new ads to setup the sting. He knows which nrs they use, how they approach you etc etc. We wanted to post the ads already but Chris has indicated that they will phone literally the next day, and pressure us to meet them that same day. So we are holding back on posting the ads until we are ready with the police.

We are planning on shooting the case studies on monday this week 8 Oct as well as recreations and the briefing with the police.

If the sting falls through I am confident that there is enough evidence and statements from our case studies, including existing SAPS case numbers for us to at least convince police to go to the house and search it.

We also have very clear CCTV images of three of the suspects, when they took one of case studies to the Vaal Mall bank to withdraw money. We are going to share the images with the police and hopefully those same men will be at the house when we hit it.

The case studies are willing to share their experiences on camera without hidden id even though they fear reprisals and are not sure if the policemen who held them up are real or not.

The actual sting is too dangerous for us to be involved in other than filming the operation and being present when it goes down. The police unit who will help us have indicated they will need 252A permission from the NDPP (permission to entrap) but that this can be given telephonically if immediate action is required and it won't cause a delay.

The idea is for us to setup the sting using our ads and Chris, record phone calls, meet the syndicate in Van der Bijl and film with hidden cams, and then get the police to bust them at the house.

Script:


OLX Gang
12 October 2018

Voices
It’s become the new norm: we all buy and sell items on-line, and literally thousands of transactions take place in South Africa every day.

Link Mac
One of the simplest ways to sell your car is by advertising it online, however you have to be very careful. Some of the people we’ve spoken to, their dream sale ended in a nightmare.

Voice
Christo van den Berg from Rustenburg wanted to sell his bakkie in June this year, and advertised it on the popular website OLX. And he soon got a call from a buyer.

Sound Up Christo
So what happened is a guy from, claiming to come from Namibia, claiming that he wanted to buy my vehicle, but that he was in a great hurry, because he needed to leave the country and he works for De Beers mining.

Voice
The man spoke fluent Afrikaans and identified himself as George.

Sound Up Christo
And he was quite adamant that I bring it as soon as possible because he was leaving the county.

Voice
JJ Pretorius and his father Josh who are from Witbank, advertised a quad bike they had for sale on OLX just two weeks ago.

Sound Up JJ Pretorius
Mac: So JJ, lets start with you. You just wanted to sell you motorcycle right?

JJ: Yes, I’ve posted an ad on OLX to sell my motorbike, and maybe about two days later I received a phone call from this guy, Sebastian, talking fluently Afrikaans.

Voice
What the men didn’t know at the time was that George and Sebastian were in fact the same man, who we’ll call Mr X. The unwitting sellers were being lured into the clutches of a notorious syndicate who specialise in kidnapping and extortion. Although the incidents took place months apart, the gang’s Modus Operandi stays exactly the same. In a three part scam, victims are lured to Van der Bijl Park by Mr X, who then introduces them to a second member of the syndicate who shows them a cooler bag full of cash and diamonds. The syndicate explains that the diamonds are to be sold to a third party to make up the rest of the cash to purchase their vehicle. Mr X then accompanies the victims to a house in the neighbouring township of Evaton, where they are told to wait for the money to arrive.

Sound Up JJ
JJ: And when we got to the house he told us to sit down, get comfortable, he will pay us just now.

Voice
Then it’s time for part two of the scam. Armed men, dressed in police uniforms, barge into the house and accuse the innocent victims of illicit diamond dealings.

Sound Up Josh
When these two police men came in with the uniforms, they just shouted at us, what are you guys doing here, what are you guys doing here?

Voice
The same thing happened to van den Berg and a friend who had accompanied him to Van der Bijl.

Sound Up Christo
The police barged in there, pointing the guns in our faces, shouting at us.

Voice
Part three of the scam involves victims being split up into separate rooms. The uniformed police disappear off the scene and are replaced by supposed plain clothes detectives - and then the threats begin.

Sound Up Josh
And then they said these diamonds are valued at over R1.3m, do we know what is our bail?

Sound Up Christo
They would lock us up for the whole weekend, and they guaranteed us that we would get raped as many times as needed if we didn’t work with their plan that they had with us.

Sound Up Josh
I told them, please, for the last time, take us to the police station. That’s where the guy came up with a gun, and he pushed it into my mouth, and my gums started bleeding, he says to me: you got your last chance now.

Voice
The scam’s finale’ involves extorting money from the victims by warning them that the threats are about to become a reality.

Sound Up Christo
So they then requested us to show us how much money we had in our accounts on our mobile apps, they then transferred the money, and what they couldn’t transfer they then forced the pin codes out of us, and then we had to hand over our cards, and they then withdrew everything that they could for that day.

Voice
Josh Pretorius says he was forced into this red Volkswagen Golf, and driven to a bank.

Sound Up Josh
And we went back to Van der Bijl, to the Vaal Mall. And the whole time when I was sitting at the back they said to me Oupa, remember if you’re going to try anything now, as from now on, remember we’ve got your son. We’ve got him locked up. We’ll take him out, you’ll never see your son. So a lot of things went through my mind. I just thought, you know, we won’t get out of here today. I have to cooperate with them.

Voice
This CCTV footage shows the Golf arriving at the mall. In order to help the police achieve successful prosecutions, we are hiding the faces of the suspects. The gang told Pretorius to enter the bank and withdraw all the money in his account.

Sound Up Josh
Josh: It was very busy, they couldn’t get parking, so there we stop now.

Mac: And these guys, they’re relaxed, they’re not worried about police, nothing…

Josh: Very, very relaxed.

Mac: So this is you entering into the mall now?

Josh: There I’m entering into the mall now, and you’ll see the other guy, he walked behind me, there he’s coming, to show me I must go into that door there.

Voice
Pretorius says this footage shows two more members of the syndicate standing outside the bank.

Sound Up Josh
That’s the two captains, they call themselves captains. They were watching me the whole time, I couldn’t do any move.

Voice
Combined, our case studies lost close to a R100 000 in the two separate incidents. After hours of being held hostage they were all eventually let go, but not before a final ominous threat from the gangsters.

Sound Up Christo
He explained to us nicely, if you guys go to the nearest police station now, we will take you out.

Voice
Despite the threats, our case studies did lay charges with the police, but van den Berg says it’s difficult to know who to trust.

Sound Up Christo
Even the guys that phoned me to follow up on the case, I don’t know if it’s the good guys or the bad guys. I don’t know what should I tell them, what shouldn’t I tell them. Because in some of the cases people have been asked to go and identify people but I know they didn’t go because they are scared.

Voice
A bit of online research revealed that the scam has been going on for years, across multiple platforms, not just OLX. Our producers decided it was time to catch the gang at their own game, and on tuesday this week we placed our own ads on-line. The very next day we got a call from a man who identified himself as James. And surprise-surprise, James spoke Afrikaans, also claimed to be from Namibia, and said he was in the diamond industry.

Sound Up Phonecall
James: My name is James, and I’m not from this country, I come from Namibia.

Producer: From Namibia?

James: Ja, I work for De Beers with diamonds.

Voice
We replayed the audio from the phonecall to our case studies and they confirmed James was the same man who had contacted them - Mr X had taken the bait. So we approached the police’s National Crime Intelligence with our information. Bright and early on thursday morning this week we met up with members of both Crime Intelligence and a specialist SAPS unit known as the Gauteng Specific Crimes Trio, in Krugersdorp.

Sound Up Mac
So the syndicate has contacted us and now we’re with the specialist police unit out in Krugersdorp. And we’re going to make our way to Vereeniging to do the sting operation and catch these guys.

Voice
Our next stop was at an undisclosed location in Vereeniging near where we had agreed to meet Mr X. Due to the sensitive nature of their work, we’ve blurred some of the faces and registration numbers of the policemen involved in the operation. As this footage shows, they weren’t planning on taking any chances with the syndicate.

Sound Up Mac
It is a bit scary, but hopefully we’ll be able to do a good job.

Voice
Two undercover agents played the part of our would be sellers. As they left to meet Mr X, our team joined the rest of the police vehicles who would follow the action at a discreet distance.

Sound Up Mac
As you can see communication is quite important in these kind of things, all the different units and all the different cars are communicating with each other, trying to find out exactly where the suspect is. They’re also quite wary that they could be followed or that something could be happening so it’s a very delicate process.

Voice
This dash-cam fooatge shows Mr X, seen here, waiting to meet the undercover agents before climbing into the car with them.

Voice
At the same time, the police units nearby, who had been closely monitoring the situation, spotted a suspicious looking silver Golf GTI with three men inside who seemed to be following the undercover agents.

Sound Up Police radio
Ok I also cannot go near them anymore because they see me.

Voice
Not knowing whether the men were armed or not, or what their intentions were, the police decided to end the sting operation and arrest the suspects right then and there.

Sound Up Mac
It’s three suspects that have been found, they were found with the money here. And they have been scouting the area for quite some time now, and fortunately police have been able to catch them while they were in the act.

Voice
Just a few blocks away, the second team of police had successfully apprehended Mr X, aka George, aka Sebastian, aka James.

Sound Up Mac
Fortunately they were able to apprehend him in one of the streets here in Vereeniging. But this is part of the guys that have been stealing and taking money from unsuspecting people that are just trying to sell their cars on the internet.

Voice
Mr X and the three men from the golf were taken to to the Van der Bijl Park police station to be charged.

Sound Up Mac
So the forensics unit has now arrived. What they are now doing is going through the entire car which the suspects were using.

Voice
The bag of cash victims were lured with turned out to be nothing more than packs of card board with a single R100 note on top, and the diamonds were fakes. But the police weren’t finished for the day. We travelled with them to Evaton, where they wanted to search one of the houses the gang had used in the scam.

Sound Up Mac
So we’ve just arrived at one of the houses where people are normally brought to, this is where money is extorted from them. There’s a couple of them around the Vaal area, but this is the one we’ve gone into to see and try and find out what is happening here.

Voice
The search revealed no new evidence, but this man who could not give any satisfactory answers as to how he afforded the house or his BMW, was also arrested. On friday, SAPS spokesperson Lieutenant Colonel Lungelo Dlamini gave us this statement.

Sound Up Col Dlamini
An operation by Gauteng Specific Crimes Unit, and the National Crime Intelligence, lead to the arrest of a group of five suspects believed to be part of a syndicate. All the suspects, who are namibian nationals, are due to appear in Van der Bijl Park Magistrate’s court on charges of robbery, kidnapping and assault.

Voice
In a written response, OLX said: “The safety of our customers is extremely important to us…We invest heavily in technology to detect fraudulent users and cooperate with SAPS to bring perpetrators to book.” Van den Berg says the best way to safeguard yourself is to do your homework before you ever meet with a buyer or seller.

Sound Up Chris
Get their details, look them up on Facebook, go and search their number on Linked-In. There are so many platforms where you can actually see if this guy is legitimate. If you can’t get anything off him, and he doesn’t have a whats-app line, he’s definitely trying to con you.





















Promos

30 sec

Sound Up Police
Uncle, put your hands behind your back.

Voice
We join forces with a specialised police unit in a risky undercover sting operation, to bring a dangerous criminal syndicate that robs, kidnaps and extorts money from innocent victims to it’s knees. (12 Sec)

Sound Up Josh
They said to me Oupa, remember if you’re going to try anything now, as from now on, remember we’ve got your son.

Voice
How does selling your car online lead you into a trap involving illicit diamonds, fake money, and being held at gunpoint? (8 sec)




Promo 15 sec

Sound Up Christo
The police barged in there, pointing the guns in our faces, shouting at us.

Voice
Unsuspecting online vehicle sellers end up in the hands of ruthless criminals who pose as police and diamond smugglers to clean out their victims bank accounts. (10 sec)


Promo 15 sec B

Voice
We go undercover with a specialist police unit to arrest a dangerous criminal syndicate. (5 sec)

Sound Up Josh
That’s where the guy came up with a gun, and he pushed it into my mouth, and my gums started bleeding,


Promo 10 sec
We engineer a sting to take down a criminal syndicate who lure innocent online vehicle sellers into a dark web of robbery, kidnapping and extortion (10 sec)

Sound Up Christo They would lock us up for the whole weekend, and they guaranteed us that we would get raped as many times as needed if we didn’t work with their plan that they had with us. Sound Up Josh I told them, please, for the last time, take us to the police station. That’s where the guy came up with a gun, and he pushed it into my mouth, and my gums started bleeding, he says to me: you got your last chance now. Voice The scam’s finale’ involves extorting money from the victims by warning them that the threats are about to become a reality. Sound Up Christo So they then requested us to show us how much money we had in our accounts on our mobile apps, they then transferred the money, and what they couldn’t transfer they then forced the pin codes out of us, and then we had to hand over our cards, and they then withdrew everything that they could for that day. Voice Josh Pretorius says he was forced into this red Volkswagen Golf, and driven to a bank. Sound Up Josh And we went back to Van der Bijl, to the Vaal Mall. And the whole time when I was sitting at the back they said to me Oupa, remember if you’re going to try anything now, as from now on, remember we’ve got your son. We’ve got him locked up. We’ll take him out, you’ll never see your son. So a lot of things went through my mind. I just thought, you know, we won’t get out of here today. I have to cooperate with them. Voice This CCTV footage shows the Golf arriving at the mall. In order to help the police achieve successful prosecutions, we are hiding the faces of the suspects. The gang told Pretorius to enter the bank and withdraw all the money in his account. Sound Up Josh Josh: It was very busy, they couldn’t get parking, so there we stop now. Mac: And these guys, they’re relaxed, they’re not worried about police, nothing… Josh: Very, very relaxed. Mac: So this is you entering into the mall now? Josh: There I’m entering into the mall now, and you’ll see the other guy, he walked behind me, there he’s coming, to show me I must go into that door there. Voice Pretorius says this footage shows two more members of the syndicate standing outside the bank. Sound Up Josh That’s the two captains, they call themselves captains. They were watching me the whole time, I couldn’t do any move. Voice Combined, our case studies lost close to a R100 000 in the two separate incidents. After hours of being held hostage they were all eventually let go, but not before a final ominous threat from the gangsters. Sound Up Christo He explained to us nicely, if you guys go to the nearest police station now, we will take you out. Voice Despite the threats, our case studies did lay charges with the police, but van den Berg says it’s difficult to know who to trust. Sound Up Christo Even the guys that phoned me to follow up on the case, I don’t know if it’s the good guys or the bad guys. I don’t know what should I tell them, what shouldn’t I tell them. Because in some of the cases people have been asked to go and identify people but I know they didn’t go because they are scared. Voice A bit of online research revealed that the scam has been going on for years, across multiple platforms, not just OLX. Our producers decided it was time to catch the gang at their own game, and on tuesday this week we placed our own ads on-line. The very next day we got a call from a man who identified himself as James. And surprise-surprise, James spoke Afrikaans, also claimed to be from Namibia, and said he was in the diamond industry. Sound Up Phonecall James: My name is James, and I’m not from this country, I come from Namibia. Producer: From Namibia? James: Ja, I work for De Beers with diamonds. Voice We replayed the audio from the phonecall to our case studies and they confirmed James was the same man who had contacted them - Mr X had taken the bait. So we approached the police’s National Crime Intelligence with our information. Bright and early on thursday morning this week we met up with members of both Crime Intelligence and a specialist SAPS unit known as the Gauteng Specific Crimes Trio, in Krugersdorp. Sound Up Mac So the syndicate has contacted us and now we’re with the specialist police unit out in Krugersdorp. And we’re going to make our way to Vereeniging to do the sting operation and catch these guys. Voice Our next stop was at an undisclosed location in Vereeniging near where we had agreed to meet Mr X. Due to the sensitive nature of their work, we’ve blurred some of the faces and registration numbers of the policemen involved in the operation. As this footage shows, they weren’t planning on taking any chances with the syndicate. Sound Up Mac It is a bit scary, but hopefully we’ll be able to do a good job. Voice Two undercover agents played the part of our would be sellers. As they left to meet Mr X, our team joined the rest of the police vehicles who would follow the action at a discreet distance. Sound Up Mac As you can see communication is quite important in these kind of things, all the different units and all the different cars are communicating with each other, trying to find out exactly where the suspect is. They’re also quite wary that they could be followed or that something could be happening so it’s a very delicate process. Voice This dash-cam fooatge shows Mr X, seen here, waiting to meet the undercover agents before climbing into the car with them. Voice At the same time, the police units nearby, who had been closely monitoring the situation, spotted a suspicious looking silver Golf GTI with three men inside who seemed to be following the undercover agents. Sound Up Police radio Ok I also cannot go near them anymore because they see me. Voice Not knowing whether the men were armed or not, or what their intentions were, the police decided to end the sting operation and arrest the suspects right then and there. Sound Up Mac It’s three suspects that have been found, they were found with the money here. And they have been scouting the area for quite some time now, and fortunately police have been able to catch them while they were in the act. Voice Just a few blocks away, the second team of police had successfully apprehended Mr X, aka George, aka Sebastian, aka James. Sound Up Mac Fortunately they were able to apprehend him in one of the streets here in Vereeniging. But this is part of the guys that have been stealing and taking money from unsuspecting people that are just trying to sell their cars on the internet. Voice Mr X and the three men from the golf were taken to to the Van der Bijl Park police station to be charged. Sound Up Mac So the forensics unit has now arrived. What they are now doing is going through the entire car which the suspects were using. Voice The bag of cash victims were lured with turned out to be nothing more than packs of card board with a single R100 note on top, and the diamonds were fakes. But the police weren’t finished for the day. We travelled with them to Evaton, where they wanted to search one of the houses the gang had used in the scam. Sound Up Mac So we’ve just arrived at one of the houses where people are normally brought to, this is where money is extorted from them. There’s a couple of them around the Vaal area, but this is the one we’ve gone into to see and try and find out what is happening here. Voice The search revealed no new evidence, but this man who could not give any satisfactory answers as to how he afforded the house or his BMW, was also arrested. On friday, SAPS spokesperson Lieutenant Colonel Lungelo Dlamini gave us this statement. Sound Up Col Dlamini An operation by Gauteng Specific Crimes Unit, and the National Crime Intelligence, lead to the arrest of a group of five suspects believed to be part of a syndicate. All the suspects, who are namibian nationals, are due to appear in Van der Bijl Park Magistrate’s court on charges of robbery, kidnapping and assault. Voice In a written response, OLX said: “The safety of our customers is extremely important to us…We invest heavily in technology to detect fraudulent users and cooperate with SAPS to bring perpetrators to book.” Van den Berg says the best way to safeguard yourself is to do your homework before you ever meet with a buyer or seller. Sound Up Chris Get their details, look them up on Facebook, go and search their number on Linked-In. There are so many platforms where you can actually see if this guy is legitimate. If you can’t get anything off him, and he doesn’t have a whats-app line, he’s definitely trying to con you. Promos 30 sec Sound Up Police Uncle, put your hands behind your back. Voice We join forces with a specialised police unit in a risky undercover sting operation, to bring a dangerous criminal syndicate that robs, kidnaps and extorts money from innocent victims to it’s knees. (12 Sec) Sound Up Josh They said to me Oupa, remember if you’re going to try anything now, as from now on, remember we’ve got your son. Voice How does selling your car online lead you into a trap involving illicit diamonds, fake money, and being held at gunpoint? (8 sec) Promo 15 sec Sound Up Christo The police barged in there, pointing the guns in our faces, shouting at us. Voice Unsuspecting online vehicle sellers end up in the hands of ruthless criminals who pose as police and diamond smugglers to clean out their victims bank accounts. (10 sec) Promo 15 sec B Voice We go undercover with a specialist police unit to arrest a dangerous criminal syndicate. (5 sec) Sound Up Josh That’s where the guy came up with a gun, and he pushed it into my mouth, and my gums started bleeding, Promo 10 sec We engineer a sting to take down a criminal syndicate who lure innocent online vehicle sellers into a dark web of robbery, kidnapping and extortion (10 sec)

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We expose a dangerous syndicate who hold innocent victims who advertised vehicles for sale online, hostage at gunpoint and force them to empty out their bank accounts.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We have been approached by two case studies who have fallen victim to a syndicate using the exact same modus operandi to rob them. The syndicate approaches people who have advertised vehicles for sale online via sites like OLX and Gumtree. They employ the exact same tactics every time. A coloured man who speaks fluent afrikaans phones the victim, and he claims to be in South Africa from Namibia. He offers to buy the vehicle at the advertised price, but tells the victims they have to meet him in Van der Bijl Park as he is only in the country for a short time and does not have transport. He assures them he does not need to see the vehicle, and that he is a truck driver, and will come pick up the vehicle with the truck on the next visit to SA.
metadata.Summary: He asks them to remove the ads online. He tells them to meet him at a shopping center in Van der Bijl Park where they can sign a sales contract and he will pay the money over to their accounts. Once they meet him at the shopping centre the story changes. He shows them a large amount of cash, and says he will pay them cash, but that they have to go fetch the rest of the money at a friend's house. They then drive him to a house (that we have identified) in Evaton. Once inside they show the victims another bag which supposedly contains rough diamonds and asks them if they will be interested in taking the diamonds as payment. At this point two men, dressed in full police uniforms appear, and accuse the victims of being involved in diamond smuggling. They separate the victims into two rooms, where they are told they will be taken to police station and repeatedly raped if they do not cooperate. They are physically assaulted and have guns pointed at them. They are then forced to transfer money from their bank accounts into the syndicates bank accounts. The syndicate also takes their bank cards to atms and withdraws cash. If the limits are reached, the syndicate will hold one victim hostage while another is driven to a bank where they are forced to withdraw any remaining funds under threat of having the remaining victim at the house shot. Once the victims have been robbed, they are let go, and warned that if they go to police they will be killed. The syndicate has their registration nr on their vehicle checked, and obtain personal info like street address and such about the victims. They are then told the usual "we know where you live"...
metadata.Further information: We have identified the house where the syndicate operates from(at least in our two cases studies incidents) We have approached the Hawks organised crime unit via Gen Mokotedi and a Col Frik Smit. They have given the green light to go ahead with a sting/ bust, but they have not responded since and don't seem to be in much of a hurry to help us. So then we approached members of Crime Intelligence, who are willing to setup the sting with us. They have a hand picked unit made up of police from different units who could carry out the sting and make the arrests. We are meeting with them on monday afternoon, we are going to film the briefing session with presenter. They are adamant that the sting can happen soon, but want as much info from us as possible. One of our case studies, Chris van den Berg, has since it happened to him posted fake ads online and been contacted by the same gang. He has agreed to help us post new ads to setup the sting. He knows which nrs they use, how they approach you etc etc. We wanted to post the ads already but Chris has indicated that they will phone literally the next day, and pressure us to meet them that same day. So we are holding back on posting the ads until we are ready with the police. We are planning on shooting the case studies on monday this week 8 Oct as well as recreations and the briefing with the police. If the sting falls through I am confident that there is enough evidence and statements from our case studies, including existing SAPS case numbers for us to at least convince police to go to the house and search it. We also have very clear CCTV images of three of the suspects, when they took one of case studies to the Vaal Mall bank to withdraw money. We are going to share the images with the police and hopefully those same men will be at the house when we hit it. The case studies are willing to share their experiences on camera without hidden id even though they fear reprisals and are not sure if the policemen who held them up are real or not. The actual sting is too dangerous for us to be involved in other than filming the operation and being present when it goes down. The police unit who will help us have indicated they will need 252A permission from the NDPP (permission to entrap) but that this can be given telephonically if immediate action is required and it won't cause a delay. The idea is for us to setup the sting using our ads and Chris, record phone calls, meet the syndicate in Van der Bijl and film with hidden cams, and then get the police to bust them at the house.
